title: Peace with God
summary: Justified by faith, we have a peace no one can buy, access to grace, and a hope that suffering cannot take away.
exhortation: I had the privilege of calling a wonderful brother in the Lord who has been battling cancer for the last year and a half. I thought I was calling to encourage him. I was the one who was encouraged. What I encountered was a supernatural faith that defied human logic, a faith so sure of the Lord and so completely trusting in his Savior that it left me in awe. He read me this passage, full of faith, and I wanted to read it to you.

"Since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ." Our greatest problem is solved by putting our faith in Jesus. We have peace with God, a treasure beyond price. Billionaires on their deathbeds would give every dollar to extend their lives, and one day it will end in gnashing of teeth because they don't have this peace. You can't purchase it.

And it keeps going: "Through him we have also obtained access by faith into this grace in which we stand." This is a hallmark of the God we serve. He lavishes grace upon grace, kindness upon kindness, gift upon gift. And so we rejoice in hope of the glory of God. We do not hope in vain.

"Not only that, but we rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, and hope does not put us to shame." Peace with God, access to his grace, and the rejoicing it produces: this is a supernatural faith that can carry you through the most intense trials of life. I saw it in that beautiful saint. If you have put your trust in Jesus, you have a peace that surpasses understanding and a faith that can't be taken from you, even in suffering. It will produce endurance and a hope that lasts forever.
prayer: Thank you for this hope, Lord. What a joy it is to be known and loved by you, and to know the depths and riches of the grace and love poured out for us. Thank you for the example of this saint, who finds hope and joy even in the midst of cancer.
Lift our eyes off the troubles of this world and fix them on you, Jesus, who gave everything so that we might be reconciled to you. Let us find our joy in this great salvation. In Jesus' name, amen.
